purpose: Pegvisomant is used to treat a condition called acromegaly, where the body makes too much growth hormone. This causes abnormal growth of bones and tissues, especially in the hands, feet, and face. This medicine helps bring those hormone levels back to normal and relieves symptoms.
how_it_works: Your body has a condition where too much growth hormone is causing problems. Pegvisomant works by blocking the places in your body where growth hormone attaches, so it cannot do its job. This helps lower the levels of another hormone called IGF-1, which is what actually causes most of the harmful effects of excess growth hormone.
common_side_effects: Injection site reactions like redness, swelling, or pain where you give the shot. Some people experience headache, tiredness, nausea, or diarrhea. You may also notice some weight gain or flu-like symptoms, especially when starting the medication.
warnings: This medicine can affect your liver, so your doctor will do regular blood tests to check your liver health. Tell your doctor right away if you notice yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, or stomach pain. If you have diabetes, your blood sugar may change because this medication can affect insulin sensitivity, so monitor your levels closely. Do not use this medicine if you are pregnant or breastfeeding without talking to your doctor first.
typical_dosing: Pegvisomant is given as an injection under the skin, usually once a day. Your doctor will start you on a loading dose of 40 mg given in the clinic, then you will take 10 mg daily at home. Your dose may be adjusted up or down based on your IGF-1 blood test results, typically ranging from 10 mg to 30 mg per day.
